statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 9% (low), Stress 49% (elevated), Confidence 88% (high), dominant mode mixed. NQZ26 trades 31,210.50 at 16:17:14Z, up 148.75 points or 0.48% on the 31,061.75 prior close, after the 31,254.75 session high was retested at 31,254.50 and rejected and price printed 31,192.25, 62.50 points below the extreme.
recommendation: Tail at 9% sits sixteen points below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Tail falls three points from the prior hour because the retest of the 31,254.75 session high was rejected rather than exceeded, highs have stepped down to 31,220.00, and the 31,192.25 print leaves price 62.50 points off the extreme instead of holding at it. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans 19:00Z to 20:15Z, covering power hour into the US cash close, which is the only remaining structural checkpoint today. Published Tail peaks at 15% in the 14:00Z hour tomorrow around the US cash open and Fed Bowman, and stays inside the low band across all 24 modelled hours.
headline: Tail falls to 9% as the 31,254.75 session high is retested and rejected, with price 62.50 points off the extreme and WTI turning down 1.04%
body:
The prior hour published Tail at 12% and named the unresolved 31,254.75 session high as the reason it did not fall further. That level has now been tested a second time and has held, and the rejection is the decisive evidence of this hour.

NQZ26 pushed back to 31,254.50 and then 31,254.75, matching the session high almost exactly rather than extending through it. Highs have stepped down since: 31,239.25, then 31,230.00, then 31,222.75, then 31,220.00. The most recent print is 31,192.25, which is 62.50 points below the session high and the lowest level since that high was first established. The last verified quote is 31,210.50 at 16:17:14Z, up 148.75 points or 0.48% on the 31,061.75 prior close, with a day range of 30,957.50 to 31,254.75 and an open of 31,059.00. Price is 44.25 points below the high, and the sequence of lower highs is the first clean one of the session.

This matters because a double top followed by a 62.50-point give-back is structurally the opposite of the pattern that defines a Tail path. Repeated extension after failed retracements requires that pullbacks fail; here the retracement is working, and it is the fourth of the session to do so. Earlier pullbacks of 114.50, 55.25 and 35.75 points all held and all were bought, but a market that retraces and then declines to make a higher high is a functioning two-way market rather than a one-way path.

Internals continue to decline to confirm. The cash NDX is 30,986.74 at 16:26:17Z, up 178.81 points or 0.58%, and its session high of 31,005.76 is unchanged from the prior hour, so the cash index has not confirmed the futures retest. The SOX semiconductor index is 13,110.02, down 0.20% on its 13,136.67 prior close, with a session high of 13,152.67 that is also unchanged. Megacap breadth has broadened modestly: META is up 2.27%, TSLA 2.12%, AVGO 1.74%, MSFT 1.53%, NVDA 1.05%, Alphabet 0.54%, Amazon 0.36% and Apple 0.24%, so Apple has flipped positive from the 0.10% decline recorded an hour ago. All eight are green, but breadth that broadens while the index stalls at its high is a mean-reversion signature rather than a trend signature. Volatility is decaying: VIX is 15.54 at 16:11:46Z against a 15.31 prior close, having reached 16.38 earlier in the session and faded back toward its 15.49 session low.

The genuine risk driver remains rates, and it is the one input that worsened. The 10-year note yield is 5.34%, up 0.052 on the day and at a new session high, in territory reported as the highest since 2007 after a global bond sell-off. The 2-year is 4.85%, up 0.015. The Federal Reserve H.15 release is only current to 1 October, where the 2-year stood at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so the live levels rest on a secondary current source rather than a primary release. Against that, WTI has turned down to 90.16 dollars, a 1.04% decline from the 91.11 prior close and a clear change from the unchanged reading an hour ago. Oil easing removes one leg of the combination of firm energy prices and rising yields that justified the higher Stress reading earlier, which is why Stress eases from 51% to 49%.

The macro backdrop is unchanged and already in the price. ISM Services for September, released at 14:00Z, printed a headline of 54.9 against 55.4 in August, a business activity index that fell 5.2 points to 56.5, new orders at 59.8, employment back into expansion at 50.1, and a prices index at 74.0, its highest since July 2022. Friday's September payrolls added just 29,000 against a 79,000 consensus, with the prior two months revised down by a combined 60,000 and unemployment at 4.2%. The resulting tension, softer labour data alongside a 10-year at multi-year highs, is the structural feature of this market, and it is why Stress stays elevated while Tail stays low. No further US release is scheduled today, so the single remaining structural checkpoint is power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, which is the published danger window.

Tail therefore falls from 12% to 9%. Every condition the calibration requires for a quick decline is present: the extension was rejected rather than continued, retracements are functioning, volatility is decaying from its session high, cross-assets are stabilising with oil now lower, and price has left the session extreme. The 10-year at a new session high is the sole reason the score does not fall into the mid single digits.

Shared Finviz context was read and rejected as evidence. The file carries a generatedAt of 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly 5.7 days old and far outside the 90-minute freshness limit, with a partial collection status and both the futures and calendar sections unavailable, which indicates the shared collector has stopped refreshing. Publication is unaffected because that evidence is optional and fails open; this assessment rests entirely on independently verified live data. Confidence of 88% reflects a complete verified intraday price path together with cash index, volatility, semiconductor, megacap, yield and energy evidence, with the only material gaps being the unavailable shared context and the 1 October vintage of the primary H.15 yield release.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 15:00Z, published Claude Tail ranged from 3% to 17% and the mapped state stayed EA_ON and green throughout. Tail sat at 3% through the remainder of Sunday's US session on 4 October, lifted into the 12% to 15% band overnight between 22:00Z and 01:00Z as the Asian session repriced, then decayed to 6% by 08:00Z. The European morning produced a 14% print at 10:00Z on a brief downside extension that failed, easing back to 7% by 12:00Z, before the US cash open lifted Tail to 11% at 13:00Z and 17% at 14:00Z on a genuine continuation bar and a new session high, then back to 12% at 15:00Z once that extension stalled. Stress fell steadily across the window from 71% at 21:00Z to 46% at 12:00Z before recovering to 51%. No Claude publication exists for the 06:00Z clock hour, which is recorded as unavailable rather than interpolated.
outlookSummary: Published Tail eases from 9% now to 8% across the overnight stretch between 21:00Z and 06:00Z, the quietest part of the modelled path, on the base case that the rejected 31,254.75 session high caps the range and that retracements keep functioning. Two conditional risk clusters interrupt that path. The first is power hour into the 20:00Z US cash close, where Tail is modelled at 12% and which forms the published 19:00Z to 20:15Z danger window, since late-session positioning with the 10-year at its highest since 2007 is the most plausible setting for a delayed directional leg. The second builds through tomorrow's US macro block, where Tail rises to 12% at 12:00Z for the Balance of Trade release, 13% at 13:00Z for the Fed Williams speech in the pre-open hour, and peaks at 15% in the 14:00Z cash-open hour alongside Fed Bowman. Those increases reflect scheduled catalysts rather than observed structure, and every one of the 24 modelled hours remains inside the low band and below the 25% block threshold. The European cash open at 07:00Z is modelled at 11%, the hour where an opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be the first genuine evidence of a changed regime.
